ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, with chord $CD \perp AB$ at point $E$. Connect $AC$, $BC$, $BD$, and $OF \perp AC$ at point $F$, where $OF = 1$. What is the length of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OF \perp AC$,\\
it follows that $AF=FC$,\\
Since $OA=OB$,\\
it follows that $OF$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
Therefore, $BC=2OF=2$,\\
Since $AB \perp CD$,\\
it follows that $\overset{\frown}{BC}=\overset{\frown}{BD}$,\\
Therefore, $BD=BC=2$;\\
Hence, the length of $BD$ is $\boxed{2}$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as AB being the horizontal diameter of the circle, with O its center, C on the upper-right arc, D on the lower-right arc, and OF the perpendicular distance from O to line AC. From the text, OF=1 and CD ⟂ AB. Let θ=∠CAB. Since AB is a diameter, ∠ACB is a right angle by Thales' theorem. The distance from O to AC equals AO·sin θ because O lies on AB, so OF=AO sin θ. Also in right triangle ABC, BC=AB sin θ=2AO sin θ=2OF=2. Since CD is perpendicular to the diameter AB, C and D are mirror images across AB, so the chords from B to them are equal: BD=BC=2.
